text: The central claim of Searle's Chinese Room argument (1980) is that...
choices: syntax (formal symbol manipulation) is not by itself sufficient for semantics (understanding)
machines are physically incapable of processing natural language at all
the human brain is literally just a digital computer running a program
behavioral indistinguishability from a human guarantees genuine understanding
explanation: Searle argues that running the right program is pure syntax and never yields genuine understanding or semantics: the person in the room produces fluent Chinese while understanding nothing. The last option is the Turing view Searle attacks; he does not deny language processing, and he denies (not asserts) that the brain is merely a computer.
